coverage.evidence: 'Every job is read and named before it is committed, and anything inapplicable is absent rather than disabled.' All 170 lines of the generated workflow were read before the first commit, and the commit message names each job with its tool and rules: secrets (gitleaks 8.30.1, GHA-01), dependencies (osv-scanner 2.6.0, GHA-02), workflows (zizmor 1.30.1, GHA-03 and GHA-04), code (Semgrep 1.178.0, GHA-05). The TLS job with SSLyze and the running-app job with OWASP ZAP are absent, not disabled: Peer AI writes them only when the config declares an environment with a URL, and this product has none deployed. Verified by searching the file for sslyze and zap - neither appears.

'The dependency job's findings are recorded with their severities, so the 19 advisories are a list in the repository rather than a number in a conversation.' osv-scanner's first run reported 19 vulnerabilities across 11 packages: 5 critical, 5 high, 8 medium, 1 low, every one marked (dev). All 11 packages are now named in the GHA-02 deferral in peer-ai.config.json - @vitest/mocker, brace-expansion, braces, esbuild, handlebars, postcss-selector-parser, serialize-javascript, source-map-js, tinypool, vite, vitest - with the counts, the fact that 18 are fixable, and that braces 3.0.3 has no fixed version. ITEM-12 carries the same list in its goal and acceptance.

'In reporting mode a job warns and stays green, and what it would take to make each job block is written down.' Only the dependencies job reports: peer-ai-security.yml:90 carries continue-on-error: true, and render said so - 'dependencies (GHA-02), reporting only'. On this pull request it passed in 9s while still listing the advisories. The other three block, and all three now pass. What ends the deferral is written in two places: untilItem ITEM-12 in the config, and ITEM-12's fourth criterion, which says the deferral is removed and the job blocks once the advisories are cleared.

'The duplication with the old gitleaks-action step is resolved one way or the other rather than left running twice.' Resolved by deleting the hand-written secrets job from pr-checks.yml, after which render wrote Peer AI's own - its output changed from 'secrets is covered by .github/workflows/pr-checks.yml, which runs gitleaks' to 'It runs secrets (GHA-01)'. So one tool does the job, and it is now a checksum-verified binary rather than a mutable action tag that also carried a Node 20 deprecation. One coverage change is stated in the commit message rather than hidden: on a pull request it scans the branch range, with the full history on the daily run.

'DEL-03's open finding on ITEM-9 and ITEM-10 is closed with the evidence that a scheduled and per-change scan now exists.' The scan exists and has run: peer-ai-security.yml triggers on pull_request, on a schedule at cron 23 4 * * *, and on workflow_dispatch, and the dependencies job passed in 9s on this pull request having read 735 packages from package-lock.json. That answers both halves of DEL-03 - on every change and at least daily - which neither ITEM-9 nor ITEM-10 could claim. The finding's remaining half, fixing each advisory within a set time, is ITEM-12's.

Every check was seen failing before it was trusted, which is why the pipeline was pushed before anything was predicted. First run: dependencies fail with 19 advisories, workflows fail with 13 findings and 6 high, code fail with 1 finding. After the fixes: secrets pass, dependencies pass as reporting, code pass, workflows still fail with 2 medium artipacked findings - so the second run also failed, and only the third passed, after persist-credentials: false. Three observed states per job rather than one green run.

The defect class was 'nobody is looking', and what guards against its return is the daily schedule plus the three blocking jobs. The specific faults found are each closed with a guard: four unpinned actions pinned to commits, with zizmor now failing the build if one returns; two persisted credentials dropped, same guard; and the advisories carried by ITEM-12 with the job reporting until then.

coverage.reason: No user journey is in scope. No file under apps/web/src or packages/core changed, and the 487 tests are untouched - verify passed in CI on this commit.
No business rule changed. The only executable file touched is a CI naming guard, and its one hunk is a comment.

No test was added or changed. The one claim this change makes about behaviour - that the flagged regex is not vulnerable - was proven by measurement at five input sizes rather than by an assertion, because a timing assertion on a shared runner is flaky.

coverage.evidence: The input boundary in scope is the filename the suppressed regex reads, and its abuse case was exercised deliberately: inputs of 1,001 to 100,001 characters built to match the character classes then fail at the final character, the shape that triggers catastrophic backtracking where it exists. Linear timings throughout, 0.04ms to 0.46ms.

What was checked is what ships: the four jobs run from the committed workflow, against the committed lockfile and the committed workflow files, with each tool pinned so a later run installs the same bytes. There is no build step or generated copy between what the scan read and what the repository holds.

Three findings of three different kinds were answered three different ways rather than uniformly: a real fault fixed (unpinned actions, persisted credentials), a false positive suppressed with its measurement (the regex), and a true finding too large for this change parked with its list and an item (the advisories). The edge case of the parking is that it must not silently cover the other jobs: checked, and only the dependencies job carries continue-on-error.

summary: Pass, all five criteria on observed evidence. Every job was seen failing before it was trusted: the first run failed three of three, the second still failed zizmor on two medium findings, and only the third passed. The 19 advisories are now a named list in the config and in ITEM-12 rather than a number, the gitleaks duplication is resolved by one checksum-verified tool, and only the dependencies job reports.
